newsitem.title: INDIA: Tax raids hurt Indian gold, silver volumes.
newsitem.headline: Tax raids hurt Indian gold, silver volumes.

text.p: Gold prices opened lower on the back of overnight losses in the world market but limited arrivals and renewed seasonal buying at the reduced level trimmed early losses on Tuesday, dealers said.
Gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) settled 200 rupees lower at 57,100 rupees per piece. It was up 400 rupees last week.
Silver opened lower but held steady during the day on stray industrial enquiries and limited inflow of imported metal.
"Overall trading volume was low on account of raids by the income tax department on the major players since last night and these raids continued today," one broker said.
